Yogesh Malhotra: 
Thank you, Mr. Manish. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to our Q2 and H1 FY27 
earnings call. Thank you for joining us today. I hope you have had the opportunity to review our 
financial results and investor presentation, which have been uploaded to the stock exchanges.  
During today's call, I will take you through the key business developments, strategic initiatives, 
operational highlights and financial performance for the quarter and half year. Following my 
remarks, we will be happy to take your questions. 
 
We are pleased to share that Gravita has delivered resilient performance in Q2 and H1 FY27, 
navigating an evolving global environment and supply chain challenges while continuing to 
execute its long-term growth strategy. During H1 FY27, our revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 
by 40%, 29% and 10%, respectively, supported by an improved product mix, operational 
efficiencies and contribution from our diversified recycling businesses. 
 
While geopolitical developments and logistic disruptions have impacted the availability and 
movement of recyclable materials, we have been actively working to diversify our sourcing 
geographies and strengthen our procurement network.  
Alongside sourcing from India and other international markets, we are expanding our presence 
in developed economies by establishing additional scrap procurement yards. These initiatives 
are aimed at improving sourcing resilience, reducing dependence on individual geographies and 
supporting better utilization of our expanded manufacturing capacities over the longer term. 
 
Our performance reflects the strength of our diversified recycling platform and our ability to 
adapt to challenging market conditions while remaining focused on profitability, operational 
excellence and disciplined capital allocation.

Going forward, we will continue to strengthen our core businesses, expand our presence across 
products and geographies and increase the contribution of value-added products as we progress 
towards Vision 2030. 
 
Before discussing our financial performance in detail, let me first walk you through the key 
strategic developments during the quarter that continue to strengthen our growth trajectory. Our 
strategic expansion in copper recycling continues to progress well. The initiatives across Mundra 
and Mandvi designed to strengthen integration across the copper value chain.  
At Mundra, we have announced plans to add 59,200 metric tons per annum of copper recycling 
capacity with an estimated investment of approximately INR64 crores to be funded through 
internal accruals. The capacity is expected to be commissioned in phases by March 2029.  
This expansion will support raw material sourcing for our proposed Mandvi plant and further 
strengthen integration across our copper recycling operations, enabling us to cater to growing 
demand in domestic and international markets.  
At Mandvi, Gujarat, work is progressing on our 29,400 metric ton per annum copper recycling 
facility with an estimated investment of approximately INR160 crores. The project remains on 
track for commissioning within the next 12 months, as previously guided. Funded through 
internal accruals, the facility will strengthen backward integration, expand our value-added 
product portfolio and support long-term profitable growth. 
 
We have approved an additional investment of approximately INR94.42 crores to subscribe to 
the rights issue of Rashtriya Metal Industries Limited against a total rights issue of 
approximately INR94.81 crores. The proceeds will support RMIL's strategic initiatives and 
general corporate purposes, further strengthening our presence in the copper and copper alloy 
segment. 
 
We remain very optimistic on lithium-ion battery recycling space, a segment poised to grow 
alongside the rapid rise in electric vehicles. As battery feedstock availability increases, we will 
scale towards higher value recovery and processing, positioning this business as a key 
contributor to Gravita's future growth. 
 
In line with our long-term expansion strategy, we have embarked total capital expenditure of 
INR1,680 crores through FY29. Of this, INR815 crores will be allocated towards strengthening 
and expanding our existing businesses with the balance directed towards entering new recycling 
verticals, including lithium-ion battery and copper. 
 
The 57th GST Council has recommended bringing electrical and electronic waste scrap under 
the reverse charge mechanism for procurement from unregistered suppliers. This will 
exponentially enhance our domestic procurement and fast track the shift from formal to informal. 
 
We are also strengthening our international sourcing capabilities. The Board will -- the Board 
has approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in the United States proposed to 
be named Gravita Recyclers USA, Inc. with an initial capital of US$50,000. The proposed entity 
will focus on setting up scrap procurement network in the U.S. and other neighbouring countries.

It is expected to support our international procurement network, broaden sourcing options and 
improved supply chain across our recycling businesses. 
 
Reinforcing financial stability, RMIL has received an ICRA stable AA rating for its long-term 
facilities and an ICRA A1+ rating for its short-term facilities, underscoring its strong credit 
profile. 
 
Coming to operational performance. Our overall operating performance during Q2 and H1 FY27 
reflected the contribution of our expanded manufacturing base, improved operating efficiencies 
and continued focus on product mix. Total volumes increased by 3% year-on-year to 52,199 
metric ton per annum in Q2 FY27.  
While the availability and movement of scrap continued to influence operating levels in certain 
businesses, we remain focused on optimizing production, maintaining profitability and 
improving the utilization of our manufacturing facilities. 
 
Production and sales also recorded sequential growth during Q2 FY27. Value-added products 
contributed 64% of total sales in H1 FY27, reflecting continued progress in improving the 
product mix. The Plastics segment continued its strong growth momentum in Q2 FY27, driven 
by sustained demand and improved operational performance.  
The Copper segment operated at 50% capacity utilization during H1 FY27 with sales increasing 
by 12%, following our strategic entry into copper through RMIL. We are focused on improving 
operational integration, leveraging procurement and manufacturing synergies and progressively 
scaling the business.  
Our capacity utilization -- as capacity utilization improves and our planned recycling 
infrastructure comes on stream, we expect copper to become an increasingly important 
contributor to our consolidated performance. In terms of profitability, EBITDA per ton for the 
lead, aluminum, plastic and copper segment stood at INR22,620, INR22,664, INR10,334 and 
INR84,671, respectively, during Q2 FY27.  
Moving to the consolidated financial performance for Q2 FY27, revenue grew by 38% year-on-
year to INR1,427 crores, supported by the contribution from our diversified businesses, higher 
capacity utilization across key segments and continued operational efficiencies. Value-added 
products contributed 64% of consolidated revenue during the period, marking further progress 
towards our Vision 2030 target and deriving approximately 60% plus of revenue from value-
added offerings.  
RMIL contributed INR420 crores to consolidated revenue during Q2 FY27 with an EBITDA 
margin of 8.5%. Its contribution strengthens our presence in the copper and copper alloy segment 
and further diversifies our revenue base beyond our traditional recycling businesses. Adjusted 
EBITDA increased 28% year-on-year to INR143.37 crores, with EBITDA margin remaining 
healthy at over 10%. Consolidated PAT grew 6% year-on-year to INR102 crores, while PAT 
margin remained over 7%.

long-term growth trajectory. Our priorities remain clear, strengthening our leadership in core 
recycling businesses, expanding into high-growth verticals, increasing the contribution of value-
added products and building a more resilient international sourcing network.  
With a strong pipeline of capacity additions, deeper integration across the copper value chain, 
the development of lithium-ion battery recycling capabilities and continued emphasis on 
operational excellence and capital discipline, we believe Gravita is well positioned to capitalize 
on the growing global circular economy opportunity and create sustainable long-term value for 
our stakeholders.
